title: Numeric search filters fail on PostgreSQL psycopg v3 because values were bound as strings
answers: Why do run start_time or MCP created_at filters fail with a type mismatch on PostgreSQL with psycopg3?
Filtering runs by timestamp errors out on Postgres psycopg v3 with VARCHAR vs integer
Numeric attribute filter returns an error when the database is PostgreSQL using psycopg3
How does SearchUtils parse numeric attribute values for search?
body:
Symptom: On PostgreSQL with the psycopg v3 driver, searching runs by start_time, or MCP registry searches by created_at, with a numeric filter (e.g. `attributes.start_time = 1234`) fails because the value reaches an integer column as a string.
Root cause: mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:SearchUtils._get_value returned `token.value` unchanged for numeric tokens, so every numeric attribute value stayed a Python str.
Fix pattern: Convert numeric tokens inside `_get_value` once, at parse time: `int` for Integer literal tokens, `float` otherwise. Downstream code then only calls `int()` on values that are still strings (guarded by `isinstance(value, str)`) in the in-memory matchers.
Constraints: This covers every SearchUtils subclass that inherits the shared parser (runs, experiments, datasets, logged models, MCP servers/versions/endpoints). Experiment and dataset builders need extra handling (see the integer-only guard note). Test PostgreSQL paths with psycopg3 when changing this.
applies: Parsing of numeric attribute tokens in MLflow search filters for tracking and MCP registry stores; not for tag, param or metric comparisons, which are string-valued.
says: Filtering experiment runs by start time fails with a type error on PostgreSQL databases.
Searching the registry by creation timestamp crashes when using numeric filter expressions.
Support numeric attribute queries in the experiment run search bar for Postgres backends.
Timestamp comparison filters in the registry search box produce database type mismatch errors.
search: SearchUtils._get_value in mlflow/utils/search_utils.py must parse numeric tokens into int for Integer literals and float otherwise, instead of returning token.value as a string. Leaving numeric attribute tokens as strings causes type mismatch errors on PostgreSQL with the psycopg v3 driver when filtering integer columns such as start_time for runs or created_at for MCP registry entities. Downstream in-memory matchers in SearchUtils._does_run_match_clause must guard int() conversions with isinstance(value, str). This shared parser applies to runs, experiments, datasets, logged models, and MCP stores, but does not apply to string-valued tag, param, or metric comparisons.
